# Spec: scoped-fr-citations
<!-- Generated by /hefesto:hef.spec -->
<!-- Date: 2026-11-06 -->
<!-- Board item: HEF-3 — namespace FR ids per spec in req-coverage -->
<!-- req-coverage: scoped -->

## Overview

`FR-NNN` ids repeat across specs (every spec has an `FR-001`), and `speckit-helper.sh req-coverage`
matches them lexically, so one test citing `FR-004` covers every spec that declares an `FR-004`.
Measured on this repository before the change: `req-coverage --all` reports 15 shipped specs green while
each run lists 10–33 ids "declared by other specs" — the collision is what keeps several of them green.
This feature adds a spec-qualified citation, `<spec>/FR-NNN`, that counts for the named spec only, and a
per-spec opt-in to strict scoping, so new specs cannot be covered by another spec's tests while the
specs already shipped (here and in adopters' CI) stay green without a migration.

## Decisions (made here, from the code — no clarification needed)

- **D1 — the form is `<spec>/FR-NNN`** (e.g. `scoped-fr-citations/FR-003`), where `<spec>` is the
  directory name under `.specify/specs/` of the spec root `req-coverage` runs in. The path-scoping
  alternative (a bare `FR-004` counts only from tests under a path the spec names) was rejected: this
  repository's checks for nearly every spec live in one shared file, `tests/smoke.sh`
  (434 bare citations), so a path cannot separate them; a token can, in any file, any language.
- **D2 — strictness is opt-in per spec**, by the line `<!-- req-coverage: scoped -->` in `spec.md`.
  A *scoped* spec counts only qualified citations of its own ids. An unmarked spec is *legacy*: bare
  `FR-NNN` still counts as today (and so does `<its-name>/FR-NNN`). Rejected: making bare ids stop
  counting everywhere — it turns all 15 shipped specs of this repository and every adopter's
  `req-coverage.yml` CI red on upgrade, and attributing ~1000 existing bare citations to their specs by
  hand is a migration the item does not ask for ("keep the existing specs' coverage green").
- **D3 — new specs are scoped by default**: the `/hefesto:hef.spec` template writes the marker, and the
  command guidance that tells tests how to cite (`hef.tasks`, `hef.implement`, `hef.verify`,
  `hef.mutate`) shows the qualified form.
- **D4 — the matrix keeps its row shape**: a spec's own requirement rows stay `FR-NNN  COVERED|UNCOVERED`
  (the dogfood check in `tests/smoke.sh` and `/hefesto:hef.verify` read them); foreign citations print
  the token as written (`other/FR-007` or `FR-007`).

## User Scenarios

### US1: A qualified citation covers only the spec it names [P1]
- **Given** shipped specs `alpha` and `beta`, both scoped, both declaring `FR-001`, and one test citing
  `alpha/FR-001`
- **When** `req-coverage --all` runs
- **Then** `alpha`'s `FR-001` is `COVERED`, `beta`'s `FR-001` is `UNCOVERED`, and the run fails
- **Edge**: the same test also cites `beta/FR-001` → both covered, exit 0
- **Error / must NOT happen**: `alpha/FR-001` must never be read as a bare `FR-001` citation (a `grep -w`
  on `FR-001` matches inside `alpha/FR-001`, because `/` is a word boundary)
- Touches: `hooks/speckit-helper.sh` (`req-coverage`), `tests/smoke.sh` (Requirement traceability, `--all` fixture)

### US2: A scoped spec ignores bare citations, and says so [P1]
- **Given** a scoped spec `alpha` declaring `FR-002`, and a test citing only a bare `FR-002`
- **When** `req-coverage alpha` runs
- **Then** `FR-002` is `UNCOVERED`, the row names the bare citation's `file:line` and the form to use
  (`cite as alpha/FR-002`), and the exit is non-zero
- **Edge**: a bare `FR-002` plus `alpha/FR-002` elsewhere → `COVERED`, listing only the qualified hit
- **Error / must NOT happen**: a bare citation must not make a scoped spec's requirement `COVERED`
- Touches: `hooks/speckit-helper.sh`, `tests/smoke.sh`

### US3: Legacy specs keep today's behaviour [P1]
- **Given** an unmarked spec `older` declaring `FR-001`, cited by a bare `FR-001`
- **When** `req-coverage older` runs
- **Then** `FR-001` is `COVERED` exactly as before, and the header names the mode (`mode: legacy (bare ids count)`)
- **Edge**: `older/FR-001` also covers it; a qualified citation for *another* spec (`alpha/FR-001`) does not
- **Error / must NOT happen**: running the new helper on this repository must not turn any of the 15
  currently-shipped specs red
- Touches: `hooks/speckit-helper.sh`, `tests/smoke.sh`, every existing `.specify/specs/*/spec.md` (unchanged)

### US4: Foreign and broken qualified citations [P1]
- **Given** spec `mine` under check, and tests citing `older/FR-007` (declared by `older`),
  `older/<an id older does not declare>`, `mine/<an id mine does not declare>`, and `ghost/FR-001`
  (no spec `ghost`)
- **When** `req-coverage mine` runs
- **Then** `older/FR-007` is `ELSEWHERE` (exit unaffected); the two undeclared-id citations and
  `ghost/FR-001` are `UNKNOWN` and the run fails
- **Note**: every `FR-<digits>` token in a `spec.md` is read as a declaration (`speckit-helper.sh:463`),
  so specs — this one included — write example ids in prose with a non-digit placeholder
- **Edge**: the bare `ELSEWHERE` case (a bare `FR-007` that only `older` declares) is unchanged
- **Error / must NOT happen**: a qualified citation naming a non-existent spec must not be silently ignored
- Touches: `hooks/speckit-helper.sh`, `tests/smoke.sh` (ELSEWHERE fixture)

### US5: The form is documented where people look [P2]
- **Given** a person reading `docs/sdd.md` "Why `/hefesto:hef.verify` exists" and "After shipping"
- **When** they look up how a test cites a requirement
- **Then** they find the qualified form, the scoped marker, the legacy mode, and how to move a legacy spec
  to scoped (add the marker, qualify its citations, re-run `req-coverage <spec>`)
- Touches: `docs/sdd.md`, `commands/hef.spec.md`, `commands/hef.tasks.md`, `commands/hef.implement.md`,
  `commands/hef.verify.md`, `commands/hef.mutate.md`

### US6: The edit-time probe names the right spec [P2]
- **Given** a test file citing `alpha/FR-001` edited outside an implement phase, with specs `alpha` and
  `beta` both declaring `FR-001`
- **When** `spec-cite-probe.sh` runs on the edit
- **Then** it names spec `alpha` only; a bare `FR-001` keeps naming every spec that declares it
- **Error / must NOT happen**: a qualified citation must not name a spec it does not qualify
- Touches: `hooks/spec-cite-probe.sh`, its smoke check

## Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-001 | `req-coverage` recognises the token `<spec>/FR-NNN` (spec = a `.specify/specs/` directory name of the current spec root, matched by `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*` — one grammar string shared by `req-coverage` and `spec-cite-probe.sh`; a qualifier that is itself `FR-<digits>` is an id list, both ids bare) and counts it as coverage for `<spec>` only | P1 | US1 |
| FR-002 | A bare-id match never matches inside a qualified token: `alpha/FR-001` is not a bare `FR-001` citation | P1 | US1 |
| FR-003 | A spec whose `spec.md` contains the line `<!-- req-coverage: scoped -->` is scoped: only `<its-name>/FR-NNN` citations cover its requirements | P1 | US2 |
| FR-004 | In a scoped spec, when a requirement is `UNCOVERED` but bare citations of its id exist, the row keeps its `FR-NNN  UNCOVERED` shape and ends with `bare: <file:line> … — cite as <spec>/FR-NNN`, listing at most 3 locations; rows without bare citations, and legacy specs, carry no hint | P2 | US2 |
| FR-005 | An unmarked (legacy) spec counts bare `FR-NNN` and `<its-name>/FR-NNN` citations; qualified citations for other specs never cover it | P1 | US3 |
| FR-006 | The matrix header states the mode: `mode: scoped` or `mode: legacy (bare ids count)` | P2 | US3 |
| FR-007 | A qualified citation `<other>/FR-NNN` where `<other>` exists and declares the id is `ELSEWHERE` (non-failing) | P1 | US4 |
| FR-008 | A qualified citation whose spec directory does not exist, or whose spec (another spec or the spec under check) does not declare the id, is `UNKNOWN` and fails the predicate | P1 | US4 |
| FR-009 | `req-coverage --all` keeps its skip rule (open tasks → in progress), summary line, and exit contract; each spec is checked in its own mode | P1 | US1 |
| FR-010 | On this repository, `req-coverage --all` reports the same shipped specs with 0 failing after the change | P1 | US3 |
| FR-011 | `docs/sdd.md` documents the qualified form, the scoped marker, legacy mode, ELSEWHERE/UNKNOWN for qualified citations, the legacy→scoped move, and that every `FR-<digits>` token in `spec.md` is a declaration (example ids in prose need a non-digit placeholder) | P2 | US5 |
| FR-012 | The `/hefesto:hef.spec` template writes the scoped marker, and `hef.tasks`, `hef.implement`, `hef.verify`, `hef.mutate` show `<spec>/FR-NNN` as the citation form | P2 | US5 |
| FR-013 | `spec-cite-probe.sh` attributes a qualified citation to the named spec only; bare citations behave as today | P2 | US6 |
| FR-014 | The smoke fixtures cover: the cross-spec collision under `--all` (US1), bare-vs-scoped (US2), legacy (US3), qualified ELSEWHERE and the three UNKNOWN cases — missing spec, another spec's undeclared id, own undeclared id (US4), the probe (US6), a branch-independent check that no scanned file in this repository cites a qualifier with no spec directory, and a structural check of the template marker and command guidance (FR-012) — each mutation-checked | P1 | US1–US4, US6 |

## Success Criteria

| ID | Criterion | Validation Method |
|----|-----------|-------------------|
| SC-001 | Two scoped shipped specs declaring the same id: a citation qualified for one leaves the other `UNCOVERED` | smoke fixture (`--all` collision case) red/green, mutation-checked by reverting to bare matching |
| SC-002 | Zero regressions on this repository: `req-coverage --all` → same shipped-spec count, 0 failing | run before/after on the branch |
| SC-003 | The full smoke suite passes on Linux and stock macOS (bash 3.2, BSD grep) | `tests/smoke.sh` + `smoke-macos` CI |
| SC-004 | This spec is itself scoped and its tests cite `scoped-fr-citations/FR-NNN`; `req-coverage scoped-fr-citations` is green at the end | dogfood run |
